title: CRITICAL: FLA import visible-flag decode inverted — every display object imports hidden, published SWF is blank
description: Opening either golden FLA (golden.fla / golden-v2.fla) and testing in Ruffle shows a BLANK WHITE SCREEN. Root cause: packages/core/src/fla/flash8-binary.ts visibleFromObjBaseFlags(flags) returns (flags & 0x01) !== 0, but instrumentation shows 17 of 19 CPicObjBase records have flags=0x0 and 2 have flags=0x3. With the current logic, the flags=0x0 majority (all four scene objects: 'Score: 0' text, 'Test Game' text, the player instance, the playButton instance) decode as visible=false. compile.ts then honors visible===false (zero-alpha CXForm / hidden — task 0959) so the published SWF renders nothing. golden.swf (the Flash 8 reference) renders the FULL movie with everything visible, proving NONE of these objects are actually hidden — so bit0 of this flags byte is NOT the per-object visible flag. This decode was added by task 0932 ('individual display object visible/hidden flag') which got the bit semantic wrong; supersede/reopen it. FIX: determine the real per-object hidden encoding against the flacomdoc/fla-decoder references (CPicObjBase layout) — flags=0x0 must map to VISIBLE. Until the true hidden-bit is identified, defaulting objects to visible is far safer than the current all-hidden behavior. ACCEPTANCE: loadFla(golden.fla) yields visible!==false for all four scene objects; the published SWF renders the title text, score, player and play button in Ruffle (non-blank). Related: 0932 (introduced), 0959 (honors flag in compile), 1103/1145 (symbol-timeline visible), prior blank-screen fixes 0903/0899/0885.
